search_query: curcumin AND (NFE2L2 OR NRF2) AND skin

primary_evidence.title: Curcumin Protects Skin against UVB-Induced Cytotoxicity via the Keap1-Nrf2 Pathway: The Use of a Microemulsion Delivery System
primary_evidence.experimental_readout: HO-1 mRNA expression measured by real-time PCR
main_findings: Curcumin-loaded microemulsion enhanced Keap1-Nrf2-EpRE pathway activation compared with free curcumin
HO-1 mRNA expression increased approximately 3.65-fold following treatment with curcumin-loaded microemulsion
Catalase reduced HO-1 induction to approximately 2.57-fold, supporting partial involvement of hydrogen peroxide

primary_evidence.title: Oral Glucoraphanin and Curcumin Supplements Modulate Key Cytoprotective Enzymes in the Skin of Healthy Human Subjects: A Randomized Trial
primary_evidence.biological_model: Healthy human subjects with skin punch biopsies
primary_evidence.experimental_readout: NQO1 mRNA expression in human skin biopsies
main_findings: Curcumin supplementation increased NQO1 mRNA expression in human skin approximately 3.3-fold compared with baseline
Inflammatory cytokine gene expression was reduced across treatment groups
Supplement effects on UVB-induced erythema were not statistically significant

primary_evidence.title: Curcumin promotes skin wound healing by activating Nrf2 signaling pathways and inducing apoptosis in mice
primary_evidence.experimental_readout: Nrf2 and HO-1 protein levels measured by Western blot
main_findings: Curcumin treatment increased Nrf2 and HO-1 protein levels compared with control
Curcumin treatment reduced ROS and MDA and increased SOD and GSH
Curcumin treatment increased collagen fiber formation
Curcumin treatment improved wound healing rates compared with control
primary_evidence.evidence_role: In vivo mechanistic and phenotypic support

primary_evidence.title: Protective Effect of Curcumin Against Acute Ultraviolet B Irradiation-induced Photo-damage
primary_evidence.study_type: Animal in vivo and in vitro experimental study
primary_evidence.biological_model: Hairless mouse skin and immortalized human keratinocytes (HaCaT)
primary_evidence.intervention: Topical curcumin in mice and curcumin treatment in HaCaT cells
primary_evidence.experimental_readout: Nrf2 nuclear accumulation and downstream antioxidant and photodamage-related endpoints
main_findings: Topical curcumin induced Nrf2 nuclear accumulation in UVB-exposed hairless mouse skin
Curcumin reduced UVB-induced inflammatory changes, collagen derangement and lipid peroxidation in mouse skin
Curcumin reduced ROS production, LDH release and DNA damage in UVB-exposed HaCaT cells
Curcumin activated phase II detoxifying enzyme expression and promoted DNA repair activity in HaCaT cells
primary_evidence.skin_relevance: Direct in vivo and in vitro skin evidence
